title: Book Three · Chapter 83: Sixteen
story:
On Friday, Ronan turns sixteen.

Mum wishes him a happy birthday over breakfast. Dad gives his shoulder a warm squeeze before he leaves for work.

“Dumplings later,” Dad says.

“I remembered.”

“So did my stomach.”

Ronan laughs and takes his school bag.

At the classroom door, Kai and his friend are waiting. The large bag is between them.

“Now,” Kai says.

Ronan opens it. Inside is a football. It is used, but the surface feels firm under his hands. One seam has a short white mark beside it.

“We bought it together,” Kai's friend says. “At the secondhand shop.”

“That mark was there already,” Kai adds. “It isn't a hole.”

Ronan turns the ball and checks. The seam is whole.

“Mine?”

“Unless you give it back.”

He grins and lifts it out.

“I will need players.”

Kai takes half a step backward. “I know two.”

Anna arrives with her notebook. She waits until the boys move aside, then gives Ronan a narrow blue bracelet.

“I made it.”

It is woven from cord. There is a small knot at each end.

Ronan holds out his wrist. Anna ties it gently, then checks the fit with one finger.

“Too tight?”

“No.”

“Good. Happy birthday.”

He takes her hand for a moment. The bracelet moves lightly against his sleeve.

At lunch, they take the football outside. Kai's friend makes the first pass. Ronan stops it and sends it across to Kai.

Anna and Lin sit near the track with their lunch boxes. Later, the girls walk a lap together while the boys play.

Ronan scores once and misses twice. Every time he picks up the ball, the little white mark shows beside his thumb.

After school, Anna walks with him to the crossing. She has a family evening too. They stop for a minute before the roads part.

“A good sixteen?” she asks.

“So far.”

He squeezes her hand, then lets go. She smiles and takes her own road.

Dad comes home at his usual time. Mum puts her work away. The three walk to the small dumpling place and choose a table near the open front.

There are warm bowls, steam, and voices all around them. Mum chooses her favourite vegetables. Dad orders another plate for the middle.

Ronan looks from one parent to the other. Their coats hang over the chair backs. Nobody needs to clear the dishes here.

Ronan finishes a dumpling and reaches toward Mum's empty plate. She puts one hand near it.

“Leave it.”

“I can move it.”

“So can the person who works here.”

She smiles and asks him to pass the vegetables instead.

Ronan sits back. At home, the clear space on the table is always needed for something else. Here, Mum can leave her cup beside her hand.

Dad tells them about the ordinary part of his day. It is a little story about a door he tried to pull open. He needed to push it instead. Mum laughs before he reaches the end.

“You pulled it too?”

“Only once.”

Ronan looks at the doorway of the dumpling place. It is open to the street.

“A very good door.”

“For hungry people,” Dad says.

Mum chooses another dumpling and takes her time with it. Ronan leaves the plates where they are. He listens to the rest of Dad's story while the steam rises between them.

“A very good gift,” he says.

Mum smiles. Dad lifts his cup.

“To sixteen.”

On the walk home, Ronan carries the new ball. The blue cord moves at his wrist. The road to the green door is familiar, and tonight he takes his time along it.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

seam＝缝线、接缝；bracelet＝手链；woven＝编织成的；cord＝细绳。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan这章正式满几岁？新足球原本是谁出钱买来，现在归谁？
2. Anna的礼物是什么？生日这天他们有没有取消各自的朋友和家庭安排？

## 读句子

**Anna ties it gently, then checks the fit with one finger.**

拆开看：Anna / ties it gently, / then checks the fit / with one finger.

Anna／轻轻系好手链／再确认松紧／用一根手指试一下。
